verses.zh: 耶和华的话又临到我说：
verses.en: The Lord’s message came to me:

verses.zh: 「人子啊，有两个女子，是一母所生，
verses.en: “Son of man, there were two women who were daughters of the same mother.

verses.zh: 她们在埃及行邪淫，在幼年时行邪淫。她们在那里作处女的时候，有人拥抱她们的怀，抚摸她们的乳。
verses.en: They engaged in prostitution in Egypt; in their youth they engaged in prostitution. Their breasts were squeezed there; lovers[NOTE:1] fondled their virgin nipples there.
notes: In the Hebrew text the subject is left unstated and must be supplied from the context.

verses.zh: 她们的名字，姊姊名叫阿荷拉，妹妹名叫阿荷利巴。她们都归于我，生了儿女。论到她们的名字，阿荷拉就是撒马利亚，阿荷利巴就是耶路撒冷。
verses.en: Oholah was the name of the older and Oholibah[NOTE:1] the name of her younger sister. They became mine and gave birth to sons and daughters.[NOTE:2] Oholah is Samaria, and Oholibah is Jerusalem.
notes: The names Oholah and Oholibah are both derived from the word meaning “tent.” The meaning of Oholah is “her tent,” while Oholibah means “my tent is in her.”

In this allegory the Lord is depicted as being the husband of two wives. The OT law prohibited a man from marrying sisters (Lev 18:18), but the practice is attested in the OT (cf. Jacob). The metaphor is utilized here for illustrative purposes and does not mean that the Lord condoned such a practice or bigamy in general.

verses.zh: 「阿荷拉归我之后行邪淫，贪恋所爱的人，就是她的邻邦亚述人。
verses.en: “Oholah engaged in prostitution while she was mine.[NOTE:1] She lusted after her lovers, the Assyrians[NOTE:2]—warriors[NOTE:3]
notes: Engaged in prostitution refers to alliances with pagan nations in this context. In Ezek 16 harlotry described the sin of idolatry. tn Heb “while she was under me.” The expression indicates that Oholah is viewed as the Lord’s wife. See Num 5:19-20, 29.
Heb “Assyria.”
The term apparently refers to Assyrian military officers; it is better construed with the description that follows. See D. I. Block, Ezekiel (NICOT), 1:738.

verses.zh: 这些人都穿蓝衣，作省长、副省长，都骑着马，是可爱的少年人。
verses.en: clothed in blue, governors and officials, all of them desirable young men, horsemen riding on horses.

verses.zh: 阿荷拉就与亚述人中最美的男子放纵淫行，她因所恋爱之人的一切偶像，玷污自己。
verses.en: She bestowed her sexual favors[NOTE:1] on them; all of them were the choicest young men of Assyria. She defiled herself with all whom she desired[NOTE:2]—with all their idols.
notes: Heb “her harlotries.”
Heb “lusted after.”

verses.zh: 自从在埃及的时候，她就没有离开淫乱，因为她年幼作处女的时候，埃及人与她行淫，抚摸她的乳，纵欲与她行淫。
verses.en: She did not abandon the prostitution she had practiced in Egypt, for in her youth men went to bed[NOTE:1] with her, fondled her virgin breasts, and ravished her.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “lied down with.” The verb שָׁכַב (shakav) “to lie down” can imply going to bed to sleep or be a euphemism for sexual relations.
Heb “and poured out their harlotry on her.”

verses.zh: 因此，我将她交在她所爱的人手中，就是她所恋爱的亚述人手中。
verses.en: Therefore I handed her over to her lovers, the Assyrians[NOTE:1] for whom she lusted.
notes: Heb “I gave her into the hand of her lovers, into the hand of the sons of Assyria.”

verses.zh: 他们就露了她的下体，掳掠她的儿女，用刀杀了她，使她在妇女中留下臭名，因他们向她施行审判。
verses.en: They exposed her nakedness, seized her sons and daughters, and killed her with the sword. She became notorious[NOTE:1] among women, and they executed judgments against her.
notes: Heb “name.”

verses.zh: 她妹妹阿荷利巴虽然看见了，却还贪恋，比她姊姊更丑；行淫乱比她姊姊更多。
verses.en: “Her sister Oholibah watched this,[NOTE:1] but she became more corrupt in her lust than her sister had been, and her acts of prostitution were more numerous than those of her sister.
notes: The word “this” is not in the original text.

verses.zh: 她贪恋邻邦的亚述人，就是穿极华美的衣服，骑着马的省长、副省长，都是可爱的少年人。
verses.en: She lusted after the Assyrians—governors and officials, warriors in full armor, horsemen riding on horses, all of them desirable young men.

verses.zh: 我看见她被玷污了，她姊妹二人同行一路。
verses.en: I saw that she was defiled; both of them followed the same path.

verses.zh: 阿荷利巴又加增淫行，因她看见人像画在墙上，就是用丹色所画迦勒底人的像，
verses.en: But she increased her prostitution. She saw men carved on the wall, images of the Chaldeans carved in bright red,[NOTE:1]
notes: The only other occurrence of the Hebrew term is in Jer 22:14.

verses.zh: 腰间系着带子，头上有下垂的裹头巾，都是军长的形状，仿照巴比伦人的形像；他们的故土就是迦勒底。
verses.en: wearing belts on their waists and flowing turbans on their heads, all of them looking like officers, the image of Babylonians[NOTE:1] whose native land is Chaldea.
notes: Heb “the sons of Babel.”

verses.zh: 阿荷利巴一看见就贪恋他们，打发使者往迦勒底去见他们。
verses.en: When she saw them,[NOTE:1] she lusted after them and sent messengers to them in Chaldea.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “at the appearance of her eyes.”
The Chaldeans were prominent tribal groups of Babylonia. The imagery is reminiscent of events in the reigns of Hezekiah (2 Kgs 20:12-15) and Jehoiakim (2 Kgs 23:34-24:1).

verses.zh: 巴比伦人就来登她爱情的床，与她行淫玷污她。她被玷污，随后心里与他们生疏。
verses.en: The Babylonians crawled into bed with her.[NOTE:1] They defiled her with their lust; after she was defiled by them, she[NOTE:2] became disgusted with them.
notes: Heb “The sons of Babel came to her on a bed of love.”
Heb “her soul.”

verses.zh: 这样，她显露淫行，又显露下体；我心就与她生疏，像先前与她姊姊生疏一样。
verses.en: When she lustfully exposed her nakedness,[NOTE:1] I[NOTE:2] was disgusted with her, just as I[NOTE:3] had been disgusted with her sister.
notes: Heb “She exposed her harlotry and exposed her nakedness.”
Heb “my soul.”
Heb “my soul.”

verses.zh: 她还加增她的淫行，追念她幼年在埃及地行邪淫的日子，
verses.en: Yet she increased her prostitution, remembering the days of her youth when she engaged in prostitution in the land of Egypt.

verses.zh: 贪恋情人身壮精足，如驴如马。
verses.en: She lusted after her lovers there, whose genitals were like those of donkeys[NOTE:1] and whose emission was like that of stallions.
notes: Heb “She lusted after their concubines (?), whose flesh was the flesh of donkeys.” The phrase “their concubines” is difficult here. The pronoun is masculine plural, suggesting that the Egyptian men are in view, but how concubines would fit into the picture envisioned here is not clear. It is possible that the term refers here to the Egyptians’ genitals. The relative pronoun that follows introduces a more specific description of them. Some suggest that Ezekiel uses the term in an idiomatic sense of “paramour,” which is reflected in the translation above.

verses.zh: 这样，你就想起你幼年的淫行。那时，埃及人拥抱你的怀，抚摸你的乳。
verses.en: This is how you assessed[NOTE:1] the obscene conduct of your youth, when the Egyptians fondled[NOTE:2] your nipples and squeezed[NOTE:3] your young breasts.
notes: Or “you took note of.” The Hebrew verb פָּקַד (paqad) in the Qal implies evaluating something and then acting in light of that judgment; here the prophet depicts Judah as approving of her youthful unfaithfulness and then magnifying it at the present time. Some translations assume the verb should be repointed as a Niphal, rendering “you missed” or by extension “you longed for,” but such an extension of the Niphal “to be missing” is otherwise unattested.
Heb “when (they) did,” but the verb makes no sense here and is better emended to “when (they) fondled,” a verb used in vv. 3 and 8. See L. C. Allen, Ezekiel (WBC), 2:43.
Heb “for the sake of,” but the expression is awkward and is better emended to read “to squeeze.” See L. C. Allen, Ezekiel (WBC), 2:43.

verses.zh: 阿荷利巴啊，主耶和华如此说：「我必激动你先爱而后生疏的人来攻击你。我必使他们来，在你四围攻击你。
verses.en: “Therefore, Oholibah, this is what the Sovereign Lord says: Look here,[NOTE:1] I am about to stir up against you the lovers with whom you were disgusted; I will bring them against you from every side:
notes: The word הִנֵּה (hinneh, traditionally “behold”) indicates becoming aware of something and has been translated here as a verb.

verses.zh: 所来的就是巴比伦人、迦勒底的众人、比割人、书亚人、哥亚人，同着他们的还有亚述众人，乃是作省长、副省长、作军长有名声的，都骑着马，是可爱的少年人。
verses.en: the Babylonians and all the Chaldeans, Pekod,[NOTE:1] Shoa,[NOTE:2] and Koa,[NOTE:3] and all the Assyrians with them, desirable young men, all of them governors and officials, officers and nobles, all of them riding on horses.
notes: Pekod was the name of an Aramean tribe (known as Puqudu in Mesopotamian texts) that lived in the region of the Tigris River.
Shoa was the name of a nomadic people (the Sutu) that lived in Mesopotamia.
Koa was the name of another Mesopotamian people group (the Qutu).

verses.zh: 他们必带兵器、战车、辎重车，率领大众来攻击你。他们要拿大小盾牌，顶盔摆阵，在你四围攻击你。我要将审判的事交给他们，他们必按着自己的条例审判你。
verses.en: They will attack[NOTE:1] you with weapons,[NOTE:2] chariots, wagons, and with a huge army;[NOTE:3] they will array themselves against you on every side with large shields, small shields, and helmets. I will assign them the task of judgment;[NOTE:4] they will punish you according to their laws.
notes: Heb “come against.”
This is the only occurrence of this term in the OT. The precise meaning is uncertain.
Heb “an assembly of peoples.”
Heb “I will place before them judgment.”

verses.zh: 我必以忌恨攻击你；他们必以忿怒办你。他们必割去你的鼻子和耳朵；你遗留（或译：余剩；下同）的人必倒在刀下。他们必掳去你的儿女；你所遗留的必被火焚烧。
verses.en: I will direct[NOTE:1] my jealous anger against you, and they will deal with you in rage. They will cut off your nose and your ears,[NOTE:2] and your survivors will die[NOTE:3] by the sword. They will seize your sons and daughters, and your survivors will be consumed by fire.
notes: Heb “give.”
Heb “they will remove.” sn This method of punishment is attested among ancient Egyptian and Hittite civilizations. See W. Zimmerli, Ezekiel (Hermeneia), 1:489.
Heb “fall.”

verses.zh: 他们必剥去你的衣服，夺取你华美的宝器。
verses.en: They will strip your clothes off you and take away your beautiful jewelry.

verses.zh: 这样，我必使你的淫行和你从埃及地染来的淫乱止息了，使你不再仰望亚述，也不再追念埃及。
verses.en: So I will put an end to your obscene conduct and your prostitution that you have practiced in the land of Egypt.[NOTE:1] You will not seek their help[NOTE:2] or remember Egypt anymore.
notes: Heb “I will cause your obscene conduct to cease from you and your harlotry from the land of Egypt.”
Heb “lift your eyes to them.”

verses.zh: 主耶和华如此说：我必将你交在你所恨恶的人手中，就是你心与他生疏的人手中。
verses.en: “For this is what the Sovereign Lord says: Look here,[NOTE:1] I am about to deliver you over to[NOTE:2] those whom you hate, to those with whom you were disgusted.
notes: The word הִנֵּה (hinneh, traditionally “behold”) indicates becoming aware of something and has been translated here as a verb.
Heb “I am giving you into the hand of.”

verses.zh: 他们必以恨恶办你，夺取你一切劳碌得来的，留下你赤身露体。你淫乱的下体，连你的淫行，带你的淫乱，都被显露。
verses.en: They will treat you with hatred, take away all you have labored for,[NOTE:1] and leave you naked and bare. Your nakedness will be exposed, just as when you engaged in prostitution and obscene conduct.[NOTE:2]
notes: The Hebrew term means “labor,” but by extension it can also refer to that for which one works.
Heb “The nakedness of your prostitution will be exposed, and your obscene conduct and your harlotry.”

verses.zh: 人必向你行这些事；因为你随从外邦人行邪淫，被他们的偶像玷污了。
verses.en: I will do these things to you[NOTE:1] because you engaged in prostitution with the nations, polluting yourself with their idols.
notes: The infinitive absolute continues the sequence begun in v. 28: “Look here, I am about to deliver you.” See Joüon 2:430 §123.w.

verses.zh: 你走了你姊姊所走的路，所以我必将她的杯交在你手中。」
verses.en: You have followed the ways of your sister, so I will place her cup of judgment[NOTE:1] in your hand.
notes: Heb “her cup.” A cup of intoxicating strong drink is used, here and elsewhere, as a metaphor for judgment because both leave one confused and reeling. (See Jer 25:15, 17, 28; Hab 2:16.) The cup of wrath is a theme also found in the NT (Mark 14:36).

verses.zh: 主耶和华如此说：你必喝你姊姊所喝的杯；那杯又深又广，盛得甚多，使你被人嗤笑讥刺。
verses.en: This is what the Sovereign Lord says: ‘You will drink your sister’s deep and wide cup;[NOTE:1] you will be scorned and derided, for it holds a great deal.
notes: The image of a deep and wide cup suggests the degree of punishment; it will be extensive and leave the victim helpless.

verses.zh: 你必酩酊大醉，满有愁苦，喝干你姊姊撒马利亚的杯，就是令人惊骇凄凉的杯。
verses.en: You will be overcome by[NOTE:1] drunkenness and sorrow. The cup of your sister Samaria is a cup of horror and desolation.
notes: Heb “filled with.”

verses.zh: 你必喝这杯，以致喝尽。杯破又龈杯片，撕裂自己的乳；因为这事我曾说过。这是主耶和华说的。
verses.en: You will drain it dry,[NOTE:1] gnaw its pieces,[NOTE:2] and tear out your breasts,[NOTE:3] for I have spoken, declares the Sovereign Lord.’
notes: Heb “You will drink it and drain (it).”

D. I. Block compares this to the idiom of “licking the plate” (Ezekiel [NICOT], 1:754, n. 137). The text is difficult as the word translated “gnaw” is rare. The noun is used of the shattered pieces of pottery and so could envision a broken cup. But the Piel verb form is used in only one other place (Num 24:8), where it is a denominative from the noun “bone” and seems to mean to “break (bones).” Why it would be collocated with “sherds” is not clear. For this reason some emend the phrase to read “consume its dregs” (see L. C. Allen, Ezekiel [WBC], 2:44) or emend the verb to read “swallow,” as if the intoxicated Oholibah breaks the cup and then eats the very sherds in an effort to get every last drop of the beverage that dampens them.
The severe action is more extreme than beating the breasts in anguish (Isa 32:12; Nah 2:7). It is also ironic, for these are the very breasts she so blatantly offered to her lovers (vv. 3, 21).

verses.zh: 主耶和华如此说：「因你忘记我，将我丢在背后，所以你要担当你淫行和淫乱的报应。」
verses.en: “Therefore this is what the Sovereign Lord says: Because you have forgotten me and completely disregarded me,[NOTE:1] you must bear now the punishment for[NOTE:2] your obscene conduct and prostitution.”
notes: Heb “and you cast me behind your back.” The expression pictures her rejection of the Lord (see 1 Kgs 14:9).
The word “punishment” is not in the Hebrew text but is demanded by the context.

verses.zh: 耶和华又对我说：「人子啊，你要审问阿荷拉与阿荷利巴吗？当指出她们所行可憎的事。
verses.en: The Lord said to me: “Son of man, are you willing to pronounce judgment[NOTE:1] on Oholah and Oholibah? Then declare to them their abominable deeds!
notes: Heb “will you judge.” Here the imperfect form of the verb is probably used with a desiderative nuance. Addressed to the prophet, “judge” means to warn of or pronounce God’s impending judgment. See 20:4 and 22:2.

verses.zh: 她们行淫，手中有杀人的血，又与偶像行淫，并使她们为我所生的儿女经火烧给偶像。
verses.en: For they have committed adultery, and blood is on their hands. They have committed adultery with their idols; and their sons, whom they bore to me,[NOTE:1] they have passed through the fire as food to their idols.[NOTE:2]
notes: The Lord speaks here in the role of the husband of the sisters.
Heb “they have passed to them for food.” The verb is commonly taken to refer to passing children through fire, especially as an offering to the pagan god Molech. See Jer 32:35.

verses.zh: 此外，她们还有向我所行的，就是同日玷污我的圣所，干犯我的安息日。
verses.en: Moreover, they have done this to me: In the very same day[NOTE:1] they desecrated my sanctuary and profaned my Sabbaths.
notes: Heb “in that day.”

verses.zh: 她们杀了儿女献与偶像，当天又入我的圣所，将圣所亵渎了。她们在我殿中所行的乃是如此。
verses.en: On the same day they slaughtered their sons for their idols, they came to my sanctuary to desecrate it. This is what they have done in the middle of my house.

verses.zh: 「况且你们二妇打发使者去请远方人。使者到他们那里，他们就来了。你们为他们沐浴己身，粉饰眼目，佩戴妆饰，
verses.en: “They even sent for men from far away; when the messenger arrived, those men set out.[NOTE:1] For them you bathed,[NOTE:2] painted your eyes, and decorated yourself with jewelry.
notes: Heb “to whom a messenger was sent, and look, they came.” Foreign alliances are in view here.

The Hebrew verb form is feminine singular, indicating that Oholibah (Judah) is specifically addressed here. This address continues through verse 42a (note “her”), but then both sisters are described in verse 42b, where the feminine pronouns are again plural.

verses.zh: 坐在华美的床上，前面摆设桌案，将我的香料膏油摆在其上。
verses.en: You sat on a magnificent couch, with a table arranged in front of it where you placed my incense and my olive oil.

verses.zh: 在那里有群众安逸欢乐的声音，并有粗俗的人和酒徒从旷野同来，把镯子戴在二妇的手上，把华冠戴在她们的头上。
verses.en: The sound of a carefree crowd accompanied her,[NOTE:1] including all kinds of men;[NOTE:2] even Sabeans[NOTE:3] were brought from the desert. The sisters[NOTE:4] put bracelets on their wrists and beautiful crowns on their heads.
notes: Heb “(was) in her.”
Heb “and men from the multitude of mankind.”
An alternate reading is “drunkards.” Sheba is located in the area of modern day Yemen.
Heb “they”; the referents (the sisters) have been specified in the translation for the sake of clarity.

verses.zh: 「我论这行淫衰老的妇人说：现在人还要与她行淫，她也要与人行淫。
verses.en: Then I said about the one worn out by adultery, ‘Now they will commit immoral acts with her.’

verses.zh: 人与阿荷拉，并阿荷利巴二淫妇苟合，好像与妓女苟合。
verses.en: They slept with her[NOTE:1] the way someone sleeps with a prostitute. In this way they slept with Oholah and Oholibah, promiscuous women.
notes: Heb “approached.” The verb בּוֹא (boʾ) with the preposition אֶל (ʾel) means “come to” or “approach” but is also used as a euphemism for sexual relations.

verses.zh: 必有义人，照审判淫妇和流人血的妇人之例，审判她们；因为她们是淫妇，手中有杀人的血。」
verses.en: But upright men will punish them appropriately for their adultery and bloodshed,[NOTE:1] because they are adulteresses and blood is on their hands.
notes: Heb “and upright men will judge them (with) the judgment of adulteresses and the judgment of those who shed blood.”

verses.zh: 主耶和华如此说：「我必使多人来攻击她们，使她们抛来抛去，被人抢夺。
verses.en: “For this is what the Sovereign Lord says: Bring up an army[NOTE:1] against them and subject them[NOTE:2] to terror and plunder.
notes: Heb “assembly.”
Heb “give them to.”

verses.zh: 这些人必用石头打死她们，用刀剑杀害她们，又杀戮她们的儿女，用火焚烧她们的房屋。
verses.en: That army will pelt them with stones and slash them with their swords; they will kill their sons and daughters and burn their houses.[NOTE:1]
notes: The Hebrew text adds: “with fire.”

verses.zh: 这样，我必使淫行从境内止息，好叫一切妇人都受警戒，不效法你们的淫行。
verses.en: I will put an end to the obscene conduct in the land; all the women will learn a lesson from this and not engage in obscene conduct.

verses.zh: 人必照着你们的淫行报应你们；你们要担当拜偶像的罪，就知道我是主耶和华。」
verses.en: They will repay you for your obscene conduct, and you will be punished for idol worship.[NOTE:1] Then you will know that I am the Sovereign Lord.”
notes: Heb “and the sins of your idols you will bear.” By extension it can mean the punishment for the sins.

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible.
Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing
is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- Ezekiel 23 is a series of judgment oracles

- similar in subject matter to Ezek. 16

- similar in genre to "the sword oracles" of Ezek. 21

- YHWH's reasons for judging His own people are laid out in the allegory of two faithless sisters. This literary
form is not meant to support

- polygamy

- marrying sisters

It is for shock value. It is designed to be disgusting. It is ironic tragedy, but with a hopeful outcome.

- YHWH found and took special marvelous care of national Israel

- Israel, as a whole, was repeatedly unfaithful

- YHWH will restore her (e.g. Hosea 1-3)

- Ezek. 23:35 is theologically significant, as is the PERSONAL PRONOUN'S repeated use in Ezek. 23:36-45.

- The term "Israel" can refer to

- the title of the seed of Abraham that went to Egypt during the famine under Jacob, but was turned into slave labor by a later
Egyptian dynasty that did not know Joseph.

- the Northern Kingdom, which split off from the United Kingdom in 922 B.C. This new nation of Abraham's
seed took the collective title, "Israel," for themselves.

- Only context can tell which group is being referred to.

23:3 "bosom" This term (BDB 186) occurs uniquely in this chapter (i.e. Ezek. 23:3,8,21 [with emendation]) and
possibly in Prov. 5:19. The other Hebrew word for "breasts" (BDB 994) is also found in Ezek. 23:3,21, and often in
Song of Songs.

It seems unusual to have the term "virgin" (BDB 144) in this context because this refers to the wives of
YHWH figuratively bearing His children (cf. Ezek. 23:4, 37). NIDOTTE, vol. 1, p. 782, says that this refers to
"reputable" and not "wanton" women.

23:4 "Oholah and Oholibah" Their Hebrew names are a play on the Hebrew word for "tent" (BDB 14). This is
an allegory similar to chapter 16 based on Israel's and Judah's infidelity to the covenant (i.e. marriage vow) with YHWH. Oholah
(BDB 14, lit. "her tent," which may be an allusion to pagan tent-shrines or to false temples at Dan and Bethel) stands for the capital
of Israel, Samaria. Oholibah (BDB 14, lit. "my tent is in her," i.e. temple) stands for the capital of Judah, Jerusalem.

Notice how their disobedience is characterized.

- played the harlot in Egypt, Ezek. 23:3

- played the harlot in their youth

- breasts pressed, Ezek. 23:3

- virgin bosom handled, Ezek. 23:3

- they were wed to YHWH and bore children, Ezek. 23:4

Israel's idolatry in Egypt is a recurrent theme unique to Ezekiel, see Ezek. 16:26; 20:4-17. The
judgment of Egypt is described in Ezek. 29:1-32:21.

The ADJECTIVE "worn out" (BDB 115) is meant to express that Judah is an experienced

The MT Hebrew text offers a suggested change (i.e. Qere, "what is read") to a VERB (BDB 275,

The emended text reads "Will they now commit adultery with her when she is thus?"
